inputs.text: The organizers are promoting 8 million people across more than 3,300 events in all 50 states, while officials’ silence is convenient: no one has to verify the number as the headline does its political work. The “about one million” and 600-event increase from October may be less a measure of public sentiment than an effort to manufacture inevitability. Whether the figure is inflated or simply left unchallenged, those shaping the story benefit from making a disputed estimate look like proof of a nationwide uprising. The real contest is over who gets to define public opinion.

output.main_topic: Political framing of a disputed estimate of nationwide event participation
